A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shapley/AWC approach to multimodal 3D pose estimation. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. V4 includes supplementary material that is absent from the supplied v5 PDF; this is a document difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V4 reports original MM-Fi experiments, including accuracy comparisons, computational measurements, modality analyses, hyperparameter studies and supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: V5 retains original MM-Fi accuracy results, computational measurements, modality analyses and hyperparameter studies in Tables 1–4 and accompanying figures.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain Pearson-based Shapley scoring, K-means modality grouping, FIM-weighted AWC regularization and the early learning window. Removing supplementary architecture descriptions does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MM-Fi with RGB, LiDAR, mmWave and WiFi for 3D pose estimation. Protocols 1–3 still cover daily activities, rehabilitation exercises and their combination. No evaluated dataset, population or task is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators. However, v4's supplementary Table 5 comparison against the Concat.+MLP baseline, G-Blending, AGM and Modality-level disappears, as does the qualitative AGM comparison in Figure 8. Those methods remain represented in the main quantitative comparison.

E3.justification: The S1 split, three activity protocols, MPJPE/PA-MPJPE metrics, 50 training epochs, batch size 192 and optimizer schedule remain unchanged. MLP fusion remains listed in Section 4.1 and measured in Table 2. Omitted supplementary scores and implementation descriptions do not establish a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: V5 omits the supplementary pose comparisons against AGM and input-to-prediction case studies in Figures 8–9. The main modality-combination analysis, computational analysis, regularization-strength ablations and learning-window sensitivity study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 3 retains the same standard deviations of joint predictions; these describe prediction variability rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. V5 omits supplementary Table 5, including the proposed method's MPJPE/PA-MPJPE pairs of 52.73/35.56, 52.69/32.10 and 49.57/32.66 mm for Concat.+MLP under Protocols 1–3, plus comparator results. The qualitative outcomes in Figures 8–9 are also absent.

T1.justification: The principal mathematical definitions and reasoning in Equations 1–11 remain unchanged. The omitted supplementary equations describe fusion implementations and expand the existing Shapley formula into a worked example; they do not provide a distinct theorem, proof or theoretical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: balanced multimodal regression through parameter-free contribution assessment and adaptive regularization, supported by superior MM-Fi performance. The missing supplementary evidence does not change these stated claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of modality competition, weak-modality suppression, FIM regularization and learning-window tradeoffs remain unchanged. Figure 3's revised caption makes the existing near-constant-output interpretation more explicit. No substantive applicability boundary or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: Omitting supplementary Section 6 removes substantial reproduction detail: the 81-frame RGB input, encoder widths and sampling strides, 256-dimensional projections, and detailed MLP and attention fusion implementations. Conversely, v5 replaces the promised future code release with a source-code repository link. Its contents cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 broadens its application citations, including SGFormer, Robo-SGG, DC-SAM and SafeDriveRAG. The attention architecture and self-driving attention-prediction references present in v4 disappear. The central positioning against classification-oriented modality-balancing methods remains unchanged; publication updates to retained works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: V5 makes localized introduction and related-work edits, updates affiliations and the corresponding author, and adds an acknowledgement section. The main Sections 1–5 retain their organization and largely identical prose. The standalone supplementary sections and their explanations are omitted.

P2.justification: V5 removes Table 5 and Figures 7–9, eliminating the supplementary architecture diagram, MLP comparison table and both qualitative galleries. These displays are not relocated. Main Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–4 remain, with limited caption edits and text reflow.

improvement.justification: V5 preserves the core method and main results and improves code-access information. However, removing detailed architecture specifications, MLP accuracy comparisons and qualitative evidence makes the supplied paper less self-contained and reproducible. Section 4.2 still points to the absent supplement. This is a limited overall decline because the principal scientific argument and main experimental evidence remain intact.
